markdown_report:
### Insights and directions

**Starting-point insights.** (1) Feedback favors recent, repeated interests over broad historical relevance. A recent-item residual directly tests whether local evidence improves next-item ranking. (2) Older interactions can still identify stable preferences. Preserving SASRec and initializing the residual coefficient to zero provides an exact backbone starting point. (3) Compatibility and satisfied needs are separate from similarity. Pooling cannot establish either, so gains must be described as ranking improvements rather than improved purchase utility.

**Related-work insights.** (1) [Recency-bias research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722) motivates measuring excessive recent dependence. Its findings support controlled comparisons, not a presumption that recency helps. (2) [Sampled-ranking analysis](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2021/651) shows candidate sampling can change model comparisons. The pinned candidate protocol must therefore remain the selection objective. (3) [Complementarity research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.16135) distinguishes useful relationships from similarity. Titles and descriptions support limited evidence-based probes, but cannot reveal ownership or current requirements.

These insights define three directions: controlled history aggregation, evaluation reliability, and evidence-limited suitability diagnosis.

### Framework and candidate ideas

Scores are originality/future potential/code difficulty, each out of ten; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Evidence and mechanism | Scores | Positive; negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recent mean residual | Local interaction content; scalar additive branch | 4/7/2 | Clear, inexpensive hypothesis test; limited novelty and no explicit intent model |
| Last-item residual | Immediate transition; one-item branch | 3/6/1 | Strong minimal control; sensitive to an atypical latest event |
| Recent exponential residual | Local content with fixed positional decay | 4/7/3 | Tests temporal weighting; adds a decay choice and tuning cost |
| Sparse transition residual | Training-only item-pair counts | 5/7/4 | Tests transition evidence; sparse pairs and popularity confounding |

The first three operationalize recency controls; the fourth follows the supplied history-aware transition benchmark inspiration. None establishes functional compatibility.

### Selected idea: zero-initialized recent mean residual

At 10% progress, select the simplest controlled intervention. For each causal position, average the embeddings of its last five nonpadding items and add a dataset-specific learned scalar times this pool to the unchanged SASRec feature. A recent window preserves multiple local signals without introducing an additional attention network.

```text
h = SASRec(sequence)
p[t] = mean(item_embedding(valid items in positions max(0,t-4)..t))
z[t] = h[t] + alpha_dataset * p[t]   # alpha initially zero
scores = existing_predict_score(z, candidates)
```

Train backbone, last-item, recent-mean, and whole-prefix uniform-pooling variants with identical seeds, loss, and allocated budgets. Select exclusively by pinned macro validation HR@10; report category differences and paired bootstrap intervals, acknowledging search-selection uncertainty. Compare branch removal and recent/older masking as dependence diagnostics.

Retain all four routes, `GAGC_DATA_DIR`, and trial-local artifacts. Update predictor generation and compatibility hooks together; preserve `DiagnosisProbe.run_full_diagnosis` and unavailable-data flags. Initialize added parameters without changing backbone initialization. Use only training histories for pooling and exclude padding. No gain is established before evaluation.

idea.description: Add a causal recent-five-item embedding mean to SASRec features through one zero-initialized learned scalar per dataset. Compare against unchanged SASRec, a last-item residual, and a whole-prefix uniform-mean residual.
idea.motivation: The diagnosis suggests that recent, repeated interests may provide more specific evidence than broad historical relevance. At early research progress, a minimal residual makes this hypothesis inexpensive to test while retaining the backbone's initial predictions.
idea.implementation_notes: Compute causal means with cumulative embedding sums and nonpadding counts; clamp denominators and return zero for empty windows. Use the existing item embeddings and score function, without adding an unrequested normalization or scoring change. Initialize scalars after the existing backbone initialization without consuming additional random draws. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, SASREC_EPOCHS environment behavior with effective default 200, dataset routing, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Save the residual mode, window, and scalar in checkpoints and reproduce them in the predictor writer. Expose augmented features through log2feats and optional backbone/pool hooks for diagnosis; keep view.model as the trained module. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Record branch norms and branch-removal effects without treating sensitivity as evidence of improvement. Allocate matched training budgets within the shared 43,200 GPU-second limit; report actual usage. Select using only the pinned validation macro HR@10. Ratings, ownership, compatibility requirements, and simulator traits remain unobserved.
idea.pseudocode:
For each dataset d:
    Initialize the baseline SASRec exactly as before
    Register scalar alpha_d = 0
    For each training batch:
        h = backbone.log2feats(sequence)
        e = item_emb(sequence) * (sequence != 0)
        sums = causal_window_sum(e, window=5)
        counts = causal_window_sum(sequence != 0, window=5)
        pool = sums / clamp(counts, min=1)
        features = h + alpha_d * pool
        Compute unchanged positive/negative loss at valid positions
        Update backbone and alpha_d using the matched training configuration
    Save model and architecture configuration beneath trial directory
Generate predict.py using the identical feature and score computations
Compare matched variants using pinned validation macro HR@10

originality.positive: The zero-start scalar and matched pooling controls create an interpretable experiment specific to the diagnosed recent-interest failure.
originality.negative: Residual connections and history pooling are established techniques; this is an incremental empirical hypothesis.

future_potential.positive: Consistent validation improvements could justify later work on when recent evidence should influence recommendations.
future_potential.negative: A gain could reflect optimization or popularity effects and would not demonstrate compatibility reasoning or current purchase intent.

code_difficulty.positive: Cumulative sums implement the branch with linear sequence cost and one added scalar per dataset.
code_difficulty.negative: Causal padding handling, checkpoint compatibility, and predictor/diagnosis consistency still require careful verification.

related_work.title: Measuring Recency Bias (2024)
contributions: The supplied summary describes recency-bias diagnostics and improvements from mitigation in evaluated settings.
limitations: Does not establish that increasing recent-item influence helps these four datasets.

related_work.title: On the Bias of Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Explains why sampled evaluation can change model comparisons relative to full-catalog ranking.
limitations: Does not provide evidence that the proposed residual improves the pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: Complementary Recommendation Survey
contributions: The supplied summary distinguishes complementarity, substitution, and asymmetric item relationships.
limitations: Interaction similarity alone does not establish compatibility, ownership, or a user's current needs.

related_work.title: Do Sequential Recommendation Benchmarks Require Higher-Order Sequence Modelling?
contributions: The supplied summary reports strong history-aware pairwise transition baselines and motivates a transition-residual control.
limitations: Reported datasets differ from the target categories; results do not predict target-benchmark gains.
